diagnostics.message: :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_iam_role.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_launch_template.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_eks_node_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_iam_role.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

The explicit dependency from :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng to :resource.aws_launch_template.ng duplicates the attribute-reference dependency: the launch template is referenced in the ASG's launch_template_specification.
The explicit dependency from :resource.aws_eks_node_group.ng to :resource.aws_iam_role.ng duplicates the direct attribute-reference dependency through node_role_arn.

The explicit dependency from :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng to :resource.aws_iam_role.ng is already guaranteed by its dependency chain through :resource.aws_launch_template.ng and :resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.ng, which both ultimately depend on the role.

When App Mesh is enabled, the node role receives the X-Ray write permission from :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.xray-write. :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng launches the self-managed worker nodes but does not wait for that attachment, so instances may start before the role has the permission needed by App Mesh/X-Ray workloads. Add an explicit dependency to order ASG creation after the optional attachment.

When App Mesh is enabled, :resource.aws_eks_node_group.ng provisions worker nodes using the node role, but it does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.xray-write. This can leave managed nodes starting before the role has the X-Ray permission needed by App Mesh workloads; include the optional attachment in the node group's ordering dependencies.
